title: Food systems, value chains and Indian food policy · Rung 1
subtitle: Where food comes from, who decides, and what the state itself serves
coverLine: From field to plate, and the policies that built India's plate
subject: S37
author: Dr. Harsh Maheshwari

about.why: Most proposals to reduce obesity speak to the person holding the plate: eat less, choose better. But what is on the plate was decided long before, by people who grew, stored, processed, moved, priced and sold it, and by governments that shaped each of those steps. In India the state is also one of the largest cooks and grocers in the country, through rations, school meals and anganwadi food. This book maps that system, so that any intervention can be placed where it actually acts.
about.howToRead: Read Book 0 first, or at least the sections this book names as it goes. Then read this one in order: each section assumes everything before it. Keep one packaged food you eat often in mind from the first page; by the end you will sketch its supply chain yourself.

blurb: A short book on the food system for readers who work on obesity. It follows food from production through storage, processing, distribution and retail to the plate and the waste bin; asks who decides what is available, at what price and where; and sets out the Indian food policy instruments, from the public distribution system to school meals, which were built to end hunger rather than excess.
